name: Housing-Data-Coalition/oca
what_it_holds: ETL pipeline (Python) that produces 11 deidentified CSV tables from NYS Office of Court Administration NYC Housing Court filings: oca_index, oca_causes (nonpayment vs. holdover etc.), oca_addresses, oca_parties, oca_events, oca_appearances/outcomes, oca_motions, oca_decisions, oca_judgments, oca_warrants (eviction warrants). Covers all NYC landlord-tenant cases, addresses geocoded for tract-level aggregation.
why_useful: Nonpayment eviction-filing rate by address/tract is a direct, high-frequency rent-burden/housing-distress signal that can be paired with Inside Airbnb NYC listing density to test STR-driven displacement or affordability pressure claims (gap #13/#14 adjacent).
time_coverage: Not stated precisely in fetched page; OCA records span recent years (court filings ongoing)
size_hint: 11 CSV tables, city-wide court-filing volume (likely hundreds of thousands of rows across tables)
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (attribution to OCA, Right to Counsel Coalition, BetaNYC)
last_activity: not surfaced precisely; org (Housing Data Coalition) appears active with recent repos
themes: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract

name: Justlanded
what_it_holds: Python/Playwright scraper targeting Blueground's listing API (despite the repo description also naming Furnished Finder, only Blueground is implemented), with committed sample Excel outputs (listings.xlsx, sf-listings.xlsx) containing beds/baths/sqft/price-per-month/move-in/min-stay/address/city/state/lat/lon/source/link columns. Built as an MIT-course (15.573) group project; 10 commits.
why_useful: A working, verified acquisition method plus sample committed data for Blueground furnished/corporate-housing pricing — directly on-theme (coliving/corporate housing) and a possible template for pulling comparable mid-term-rental pricing to compare against ABNB long-stay ADR.
geography: at least San Francisco (sf-listings.xlsx); scraper is general
size_hint: two small Excel sample files + scraper code
last_activity: 10 commits, course project, dated activity unclear
themes: Coliving, corporate housing, furnished mid-term rental data (Blueground, Landing, Furnished Finder, Zeus), remote-work and digital-nomad data (WFH Research SWAA, Nomad List, nomad visas)
why_all: A working, verified acquisition method plus sample committed data for Blueground furnished/corporate-housing pricing — directly on-theme (coliving/corporate housing) and a possible template for pulling comparable mid-term-rental pricing to compare against ABNB long-stay ADR.

name: awesome-alternative-data
what_it_holds: Curated alt-data list for investment research (updated 7 Sep 2026) with sections Property/Real Estate, Consumer Spending & Transactions, Web Traffic & Engagement, Macroeconomic Data. Concrete free entries: HM Land Registry Price Paid (every England/Wales residential sale since 1995, free, point-in-time by construction), Dubai Pulse DLD transaction history (free); paid entries: Earnest Analytics, Consumer Edge, Second Measure/Bloomberg, Fable Data (card/transaction panels), Similarweb & Semrush (web traffic/engagement APIs).
why_useful: HM Land Registry and Dubai Pulse are free, long-run, point-in-time housing-transaction feeds relevant to STR-vs-LTR host economics (gap 13); the Similarweb/Semrush and card-panel entries map directly to gaps 5 (engagement) and 6 (consumer spend) even though most require paid access, useful as a sourcing map.

name: awesome-real-estate

name: cmhcr
what_it_holds: R package to 'Import and Clean CMHC Data Tables' -- CMHC (Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation) is Canada's federal housing agency publishing rental market survey vacancy rates, average rents, starts/completions by CMA. Package is an import/clean client, not a bundled dataset.
why_useful: Fills the Canada leg of gap #13 (long-term rental/housing economics, host supply side) with a ready-made client for CMHC's official rental market data, useful for STR<->LTR crossover analysis in Canadian markets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal) where UPGo/strr's other repos already do STR-side work.
time_coverage: whatever CMHC's public tables cover (multi-year, updated annually by CMHC)
size_hint: small package, no bundled CSVs found
themes: UPGo (McGill) and strr R package: STR research tooling and datasets for Canada/US cities
why_all: Fills the Canada leg of gap #13 (long-term rental/housing economics, host supply side) with a ready-made client for CMHC's official rental market data, useful for STR<->LTR crossover analysis in Canadian markets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal) where UPGo/strr's other repos already do STR-side work.

A ready-made client for a public, national (Canada-wide) rental-market data source — could pull CMHC vacancy/rent series for any Canadian metro, feeding STR<->LTR crossover and housing-supply-economics angles (gap #13) without re-scraping CMHC by hand.
